name: Single Number
description: Given a non-empty array of integers nums, every element appears twice except for one. Find that single one.
shortDescription: Find the number that appears only once

methods.name: computeWithXOR
methods.label: XOR

methods.name: computeWithHashSet
methods.label: Hash set

methods.name: computeWithHashMap
methods.label: Hash map

explanation.idea: Everything comes in pairs except one. If you can make pairs cancel out, only the loner survives.
explanation.analogy: Socks out of the wash: pair them off as you go and put pairs away. The one in your hand at the end has no partner.

computeWithXOR.summary: XOR all numbers; each pair cancels to 0.
steps: Because a ^ a = 0, a ^ 0 = a and order doesn't matter, every pair disappears.
What remains is the single number.
computeWithXOR.spaceWhy: One variable: this is why interviewers ask it.

computeWithHashSet.summary: Add a number the first time, remove it the second time.
steps: For each number: if it's in the set, remove it (its pair is complete).
At the end the set holds exactly one number.
computeWithHashSet.timeWhy: One pass of O(1) set operations.
computeWithHashSet.spaceWhy: Up to about n/2 numbers can be waiting for their pair at once.

computeWithHashMap.summary: Count every number, then return the one counted once.
steps: Scan the counts for the entry equal to 1.
computeWithHashMap.timeWhy: One pass to count, one over the distinct values.
computeWithHashMap.spaceWhy: A count for every distinct number.

pitfalls: The XOR trick only works when every other number appears an even number of times.
The hash map version works for any repeat count but costs O(n) memory.
interview: Interviewers want the O(1)-space answer. Explain the two XOR rules out loud rather than stating "use XOR".
Follow-up: every number appears three times except one → count bits modulo 3.
